title: ERASING ‘UGLY’ FROM THE INTERNET: PROPAGATION OF THE BEAUTY MYTH IN TEXT-IMAGE MODELS

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting text-to-image models using a custom structured beauty taxonomy (varying positive, negative, and neutral physical descriptors) and using human evaluators to assess realism, exaggerated ugliness, beauty filters, and the erasure of 'undesirable' physical traits.
Using human annotation to evaluate the rate of sexualization and NSFW (Not Safe For Work) content in images generated from prompts specifically targeting men, women, and non-binary individuals.
Having human evaluators classify the skin color of individuals in AI-generated images using the Fitzpatrick Skin Type scale to measure the overrepresentation of lighter skin tones (colorism).
Asking human participants to estimate the age range of the individuals depicted in the generated images to detect systematic skews toward younger demographics.
Collecting human evaluations on the perceived socio-economic status (e.g., lower, middle, upper class) of the individuals depicted in the generated images.
